centralQuestion: Why did a painter accused of selling a masterpiece to the Nazis need to prove that he had forged it?
thesis: Confessing forgery challenged collaboration suspicion, but authorship needed material evidence and fraud remained criminal.
viewerPayoff: Understand how a gap in attribution made the fakes persuasive and how separating old support from new paint tested the confession.

sources.organization: Royal Netherlands Chemical Society historical archive
sources.title: Froentjes and de Wild, De natuurwetenschappelijke bewijsvoering in het proces Van Meegeren (1949)
sources.notes: Report by two court-appointed examiners, contemporary to the investigation. Dutch OCR checked against parsed passages; summaries translated, no purported courtroom transcript. Methods and observations belong to the eight examined paintings; do not generalize every fake or reproduce later simplified X-ray claims. Report combines van Meegeren’s explanation with experimental confirmation; pigment tests alone did not date these paintings. Some color reactions alone were insufficient; isolated binder, optical comparison, cross-sections and material comparisons formed the evidence.

sources.title: Theodore Rousseau, The Stylistic Detection of Forgeries, Bulletin26(6),1968
sources.notes: Art historian who interrogated intermediary Miedl; specialist retrospective account. His own interrogation is participant-linked; other reconstruction is later interpretation. 1968 retrospective account is not a contemporaneous interrogation transcript. Psychological motives, exact dialogue, cobalt-blue shortcut and universal statements not adopted.

sources.title: Anna Tummers, The fingerprint of an old master (doctoral thesis,2009)
sources.notes: Footnoted specialist research separating period criticism, material evidence, later claims and disputed retrospection. Secondary legal description uses treason broadly; narration instead says suspicion of collaboration. Painting during the trial denotes the extended1945–47 proceedings, not proven painting in1947courtroom. Some experts rejected the work; never claim unanimous acceptance.

sources.title: Een jaar voor Han v. Meegeren (12November1947)
sources.notes: Same-day court reporting quotes verdict descriptions. Original court judgment not acquired; archive OCR is reporting rather than certified transcript. OCR names/punctuation may be imperfect; exact dialogue excluded. Emmaus itself was time-barred; do not say every forgery was a count in conviction.

sources.title: Art: The Price of Forgery (18November1946)
sources.notes: Near-contemporary public reporting on changing legal position, cross-checked with later verdict coverage. Reported legal status, not original dismissal order; patriotic self-presentation is his claim, not established motive.

sources.title: Art: Truth & Consequences (24November1947)
sources.notes: Contemporary trial reporting corroborates accusation, laboratory evidence and one-year sentence. Unrelated promotional FAQ preceding the actual article excluded; identity anchored to historical body and date. Reported dialogue, money, authority count and psychological/motive claims excluded.

sources.title: Han van Meegeren schildert in1945 als demonstratie van zijn kunnen
sources.notes: Institutional metadata for an actual period photograph of demonstration painting. Metadata supports a1945demonstration, not an exact start/end date or courtroom venue. Photograph inspected via repository-independent archive page; no production use planned.

caveats.statement: Period forensic report distinguishes his explanation from experimental/material corroboration. Old support is not old surface paint. Not all experts accepted all works; stylistic motivation is historical interpretation. Contemporary legal reporting is not the original judgment or dismissal order. No execution deadline or1947courtroom painting.

hooks.text: To defend himself, this painter had to prove his masterpiece was a fake.
hooks.viewerPromise: Resolve why proving a fake helped his defense without making him innocent.

hooks.text: Can an old canvas carry a modern fake?
hooks.viewerPromise: Separate the age of the support from the age of the image.
